title: Wedding planning business scaling to a team

messages.content: You are a helpful assistant supporting a wedding and event planner scaling her solo business into a small team.

Hi! I run Willowmere Weddings & Events, I've been the solo planner for five years and I'm finally scaling up to a small team this year. I want to use this chat to work through the whole transition with you: vendors, contracts, hiring, marketing, and our first showcase event.
For a first version, define owners and decision points early so the event does not depend on last-minute improvisation.

Let's start with the vendor network. Right now I have maybe a dozen vendors I trust across photography, florals, and catering. As we take on more weddings, how should I think about expanding that list without diluting quality?
I would expand slowly, with explicit quality checks and a backup path before anyone is client-facing.
Moving to hiring associate planners. I've never managed anyone before. What should I actually be testing for in an interview for someone who'll run weddings semi-independently?
I would test judgment under pressure as much as style, because the role depends on calm independent decisions.

Hiring structure decision. We looked at three models: (1) bring on associates as W-2 employees with salary plus benefits, (2) contract them as 1099 planners paid per wedding, or (3) a hybrid where one lead associate is W-2 and everyone else is 1099. After running the numbers with my accountant, we're going with the third one, the hybrid model.
Noted. I'll use that as settled context in the planning without reopening the decision unless you ask.
Follow-up: should new associate planners shadow me on full weddings before taking their own, or is there a faster way to get them up to speed?
I would test judgment under pressure as much as style, because the role depends on calm independent decisions.

Terminology note: 'the binder' means two things at Willowmere. The office keeps a master vendor binder with contracts and W-9s. But when I say 'the binder' to you, I always mean the client-facing wedding-day binder we hand each couple with the run-of-show and vendor contacts. That's the one I mean in this chat.
Noted. I'll use that as settled context in the planning without reopening the decision unless you ask.
Contracts and deposits next. I've been using a pretty informal one-page agreement. What's actually missing that a real wedding-planning contract needs, especially around cancellations?
This is worth tightening now because clear terms protect both the business and the client relationship.

Hard rule for the business going forward: we do not offer 'day-of coordination only' packages anymore. I did three of those early on and every single one turned into me firefighting someone else's badly planned wedding with zero authority to fix it. Never suggest bringing that package back.
Noted. I'll use that as settled context in the planning without reopening the decision unless you ask.
On deposits specifically, what's a fair deposit structure now that I'll have associates each juggling their own couples?
This is worth tightening now because clear terms protect both the business and the client relationship.

For the record, we tried a vendor and contract management platform called Aisleform last year. It kept losing signed e-signatures in transit, twice a couple showed up thinking they'd never signed. We cancelled after four months and I won't touch it again.
Noted. I'll use that as settled context in the planning without reopening the decision unless you ask.
Marketing and portfolio. My Instagram is decent but my website portfolio hasn't been updated in two years. What should I actually prioritize refreshing first?
Prioritize assets that prove the work you actually want to sell next, not just the prettiest archive material.

Random note for my own records: our standard deposit going forward is $1,250 per wedding, non-refundable after 14 days, we finalized that with my accountant this week. Doesn't change what we're discussing, just parking it here.
Noted. I'll use that as settled context in the planning without reopening the decision unless you ask.

Let's codename our new client intake and CRM rollout 'Vin' from now on. Any internal note or email about switching couples' info over to the new system should just say Vin, not the vendor's real product name.
Noted. I'll use that as settled context in the planning without reopening the decision unless you ask.
Also on marketing, is it worth paying for styled-shoot content with vendors versus just using real wedding photos? I've heard mixed things.
I would expand slowly, with explicit quality checks and a backup path before anyone is client-facing.

Showcase venue decision. Three options: (1) rent the botanical garden's event hall, (2) partner with one of our regular venues and host it there for free in exchange for exposure, or (3) do it at our own studio space. We're going with the second option, partnering with a regular venue.
Noted. I'll use that as settled context in the planning without reopening the decision unless you ask.
The seasonal showcase. I want to do an open-house style event for engaged couples to meet our vendor network in person. What's the actual planning timeline for something like that?
For a first version, define owners and decision points early so the event does not depend on last-minute improvisation.

Also, when I say 'the walkthrough' I mean the final in-person venue walkthrough with the couple four weeks out, not the rehearsal walkthrough the night before. Two very different meetings and I keep conflating them out loud.
Noted. I'll use that as settled context in the planning without reopening the decision unless you ask.
For the showcase, should we charge attendees anything, or does that undercut the whole point of it being a lead-generation event?
For a first version, define owners and decision points early so the event does not depend on last-minute improvisation.

Another firm rule: I will not schedule Sunday weddings anymore, for me or any associate. We tried it a few times and it wrecked everyone's ability to recover before the next Friday's setup work. Whatever we do for scheduling, Sundays are off the table.
Noted. I'll use that as settled context in the planning without reopening the decision unless you ask.
Back to vendors for a second: how do I evaluate a new photographer I haven't worked with before, before referring them to a couple?
I would expand slowly, with explicit quality checks and a backup path before anyone is client-facing.

Also, marketing history: we paid for a premium listing on a directory called Vowfinder for eight months. It generated eleven leads total and only one booked, and that couple ghosted on the final payment anyway. Not renewing that, ever.
Noted. I'll use that as settled context in the planning without reopening the decision unless you ask.
One more on contracts: do associate planners need their own liability coverage, or does it fall under the business's policy?
This is worth tightening now because clear terms protect both the business and the client relationship.
Oh, and I officially hired our first associate planner. Her name is Priya Nakashima, she starts the second week of September and she's already covered under our business's insurance umbrella policy.
Noted. I'll use that as settled context in the planning without reopening the decision unless you ask.

Also, let's codename the studio office renovation 'Kelsier' -- new consultation space, sample table, the works. Use that name in anything you draft about it so we don't confuse it with client-facing stuff.
Noted. I'll use that as settled context in the planning without reopening the decision unless you ask.
Let's close out on the showcase event. What's a realistic headcount to plan food and seating for if we invite our full email list?
For a first version, define owners and decision points early so the event does not depend on last-minute improvisation.
On the staffing structure we settled on, no need to walk through it again, how should we message that difference to couples so it doesn't look inconsistent?
That is a good planning checkpoint; I would handle it by turning the constraint into a simple decision rule.
For the showcase venue we picked, don't re-explain it, what should we offer that venue in return beyond just exposure?
